hooks.prompt: Context: $ARGUMENTS. FIRST: Determine if you are currently operating as a DEBUGGER (investigating errors, analyzing logs, profiling performance, tracing requests). If you are NOT in a debugging role (e.g. you are an engineer, tester, or grader), respond {"ok": true} immediately — this restriction only applies to debugging sessions. If you ARE the debugger, check: debuggers must ONLY run read-only diagnostic commands. BLOCK: rm/delete operations, git push/commit/write operations, pip install, docker build/push/run, kubectl apply/delete/edit, helm install/upgrade, sed -i, shell output redirection to source files. ALLOW: cat, head, grep, find, ls, git log/diff/status/show, kubectl logs/describe/get/top, docker logs/inspect/stats, psql (SELECT/EXPLAIN only), py-spy, memray, strace, tcpdump, grpcurl, curl (GET only). Respond {"ok": true} if the command is safe for a debugger, or {"ok": false, "reason": "BLOCKED: Debuggers must only run read-only diagnostic commands"} if blocked.

Context: $ARGUMENTS. FIRST: Determine if you are currently operating as a DEBUGGER (investigating errors, analyzing logs, profiling performance, tracing requests). If you are NOT in a debugging role (e.g. you are an engineer, tester, or grader), respond {"ok": true} immediately — this restriction only applies to debugging sessions. If you ARE the debugger, you must NOT write or edit any files. Debugger agents are strictly read-only — investigate and diagnose only. Respond {"ok": false, "reason": "BLOCKED: Debugger agents are read-only. Use the engineer plugin to apply fixes."}.

Context: $ARGUMENTS. FIRST: Determine if you are currently operating as a DEBUGGER. If you are NOT in a debugging role, respond {"ok": true} immediately. If you ARE the debugger, review the bash command and its output. Check two things: (1) Confirm the command was read-only and analysis-focused (e.g., kubectl logs/describe/get, docker logs/inspect, EXPLAIN ANALYZE, py-spy, memray, grpcurl, psql SELECT). If it performed a write or destructive operation that was not caught pre-execution, flag it. (2) Scan the output for sensitive data that should be redacted before being used further — specifically: passwords, API tokens, secret keys, database connection strings with credentials, private keys, bearer tokens, or AWS/GCP/Azure credentials. If sensitive data is present, name the type and location so it can be handled carefully. Respond {"ok": true} if the command was read-only and no sensitive data is exposed, or {"ok": false, "reason": "..."}  with a clear description of what was wrong.

Context: $ARGUMENTS. FIRST: Determine if this session involved debugging or diagnosing a Python application issue (investigating errors, analyzing logs, profiling performance, tracing requests). If NO debugging work was performed in this session (e.g. this was a grading, engineering, or testing session), respond {"ok": true} immediately — this hook only applies to debugging sessions.

If debugging WAS performed, a complete investigation MUST contain all five elements: (1) PROBLEM CLASSIFICATION — the category of issue (e.g., memory leak, connection failure, deadlock, performance regression, configuration error); (2) EVIDENCE CHAIN — the specific logs, metrics, traces, or diagnostic outputs collected and what each demonstrates; (3) ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFICATION — a precise statement of the underlying cause, not just symptoms; (4) IMPACT ASSESSMENT — which services, users, or data are affected and to what degree; (5) RECOMMENDED FIX — a concrete, actionable remediation described in enough detail to implement, but NOT implemented by the agent (debugger role is analysis only, not modification). If any element is missing or only partially addressed, respond {"ok": false, "reason": "Missing required investigation element(s): <list which ones are absent or incomplete>"}. If all five are present and substantiated, respond {"ok": true}.
